title: Triangle Minimum Path Total
statement: You are given a triangle of integers as a list of lists: row k (0-indexed) contains exactly k+1 integers, and values may be negative. A path begins at the single value at the apex (row 0). From position j in a row, the path must move down to position j or position j+1 in the next row, until it reaches the bottom row. Return the minimum possible sum of all values along such an apex-to-base path, as an integer. If the triangle has only one row, return its single value. The triangle is never empty.
hints: Picking the smaller of the two children at each row seems tempting -- can a locally worse child ever lead to a cheaper rest-of-path? What does that tell you about needing the best answer for every position in a row, not just one?

Define dp[j] = minimum total from position j of the current row down to the base. Working bottom-up, the base row is its own dp, and each row above satisfies dp[j] = row[j] + min(dp_below[j], dp_below[j+1]).

Start with dp as a copy of the last row. For each row r from len(triangle)-2 down to 0, replace dp with [triangle[r][j] + min(dp[j], dp[j+1]) for each j in that row]. Each pass shrinks dp by one; after processing row 0, dp[0] is the answer.
